context: A boss reminisces about his youth sports days with a teen athlete
purpose: Teach: スタジアム/最強/青春/最大限/前進/レッド/強度/失う

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: リク君、昔はね、毎週末あのスタジアムで試合してたんだよ。
lines.en: Riku, back in the day, I used to play games at that stadium every weekend.
lines.style: Warm nostalgic tone, slower pace, slight smile in voice

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: え、本当ですか?社長、現役の頃は最強だったって聞きましたよ。
lines.en: Really? I heard you were the strongest back when you played, sir.
lines.style: Energetic teenage curiosity, respectful but excited tone

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: ははは、最強かどうかは分からんが、あれが俺の青春そのものだったな。
lines.en: Haha, I don't know about strongest, but those were truly my youth days.
lines.style: Hearty laugh, reflective and warm, gentle masculine voice

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: 僕も今、最大限の努力で県大会を目指してるんです。
lines.en: I'm giving my absolute maximum effort right now to reach the prefectural tournament.
lines.style: Determined youthful tone, slightly tense with ambition

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: いいね、その意気だ。一歩ずつでも前進すれば、必ず結果はついてくる。
lines.en: That's the spirit. Even one step at a time, if you keep advancing, results will follow.
lines.style: Encouraging fatherly tone, steady and confident delivery

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: でも先週、ラフプレーでレッドカードもらっちゃって…落ち込んでます。
lines.en: But last week I got a red card for a rough play, and I'm feeling down about it.
lines.style: Dejected teenage tone, voice trailing off near the end

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 誰でもあるさ。練習の強度を上げすぎると、冷静さを失うこともあるんだ。
lines.en: It happens to everyone. When you push training intensity too hard, you can lose your composure.
lines.style: Understanding, gentle wisdom, slow paced reassuring tone

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: なるほど…社長の若い頃の話、もっと聞きたいです。
lines.en: I see... I'd love to hear more stories from your youth, sir.
lines.style: Brightening up, sincere admiration, slightly softer voice
